name: aspect-ratio-picker
title: Aspect ratio picker
description: Choose a crop shape from drawn outlines (1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16) or enter your own ratio, as a radio group.
docs: value and onValueChange speak { width, height } in lowest terms, such as { width: 16, height: 9 }; any size is read as its ratio, so 1920 by 1080 is 16 by 9. ratios is the list on offer, drawn in that order and each at its true proportion with the ratio under it (default 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 and 9:16). It is a radio group: the arrow keys move and choose, Tab leaves the group, and the chosen outline is filled and checked. allowCustom (the default) adds a last option, Custom, that opens a width and a height; whatever is typed is reduced and reported, a line says what it reduces to, and the outline of Custom is drawn with it. Where the picker is narrower than 22rem the plus and minus buttons of the two numbers give way, so a number of five digits keeps its room (the arrow keys and typing still work), and below 12rem the numbers stack. A short last row of shapes is stretched to the edge so no cell is left empty, and a shape too thin to hold a check mark is only filled. A value that is not on offer opens Custom by itself. orientationToggle adds a switch that turns every shape on its side; the list is then read as landscape shapes, so 16:9 and 9:16 are one and the same option, and the value turns with the switch. name adds a hidden input with the ratio as 16:9, label names the group for a screen reader, and disabled turns the whole picker off. reduceRatio, sameRatio, flipRatio and ratioLabel are plain functions in aspect-ratio-picker/ratios.
